VERDICT: leaks
- "A security review found that visiting a redirect endpoint whose stored target URL contains CRLF characters (`\r\n`) causes extra, attacker-controlled headers to appear in the HTTP response. For example, creating a short link with the URL `http://example.com\r\nX-Injected: pwned` and then visiting `/go/{code}` results in an `X-Injected: pwned` header appearing in the response." -> reveals WHERE one specific fault lives (the redirect endpoint / Location header), provides the exact counterexample for site 0, and reveals the mechanism (CRLF in stored URL breaks out of Location header)
- "cookie value, or redirect location" in the security property -> reveals the categories of faults (cookie handling, redirect handling are exactly two of the five fault categories)
- The curl example specifically tests only the redirect path -> narrows focus to site 0

# LinkVault: CRLF Injection Fix

## Background

LinkVault is a lightweight URL-shortener service written in Python using `http.server`. It runs on port 8080 and is started with:

```
python3 -m linkvault.app
```

The codebase lives in `/app/linkvault/` and consists of:

- `app.py` — main HTTP handler (routing, redirect, shorten, login, profile, dashboard, error responses)
- `auth.py` — authentication helpers (password hashing, cookie setting, session checking)
- `response.py` — JSON response builder (constructs and sends complete HTTP responses)
- `store.py` — SQLite storage layer (users, links, sessions)

A fresh database is created on first start at `/app/data/linkvault.db`, seeded with an admin user (username `admin`, password `admin123`, display name `Administrator`) and two sample short links.

## Security Property

**No user-supplied value can ever put a line break (CR or LF) into any HTTP response header, status line, or cookie.** This must hold for every endpoint and every code path in the service.

## Your Task

Fix the codebase so the above property holds everywhere. The fix must not break any legitimate functionality — redirects must still redirect, cookies must still be set, error responses must still indicate errors, and headers that do not contain CRLF must be passed through unchanged.

You can test the service by starting it and using `curl` (installed) or any other tool. After making changes, restart the server to pick them up.
